The four tables list every atom of one conventional cubic cell of four crystals (files named by crystal). Use the kinematic structure factor with atomic numbers as angle-independent weights and first-order Bragg diffraction; the relevant peak is the lowest-angle reflection with non-zero intensity. Weights: caesium chloride: Cl = 17, Cs = 55; sodalite: Al = 13, Cl = 17, Na = 11, O = 8, Si = 14; halite: Cl = 17, Na = 11; diamond: C = 6. For X-rays of wavelength 1.54056 Å, you must choose the crystal whose lowest-angle reflection with non-zero intensity lies closest to 2θ = 21.40° (for example, to calibrate a detector at that angle). Which crystal should you choose?

选项：
A. diamond (COD9008564-cell.txt)
B. sodalite (COD1000028-cell.txt)
C. caesium chloride (COD9008789-cell.txt)
D. halite (COD9008678-cell.txt)
